about: The one source for /projects (2026-11-22). About 15 items in four groups. Every number here has a row in the public fact sheet. Each card says who built it and links to the live thing.

groups.title: My own builds
groups.lede: Things I built on my own time. Most of this code was written by Claude Code agents I run. I pick what gets built, set the tests it has to pass, and check it by using it.

items.title: Nerve Center
items.line: My own agent system on Claude Code. I've built 100+ agents for it since February 2026. It drafts my email and writes a lot of my code.

items.title: agent-safety-case-study
items.line: What I let my AI agents do in my work and life, what broke, and what I changed after each incident. Start here.

items.title: clawdling
items.line: Run several Claude Code projects at once. When an agent says done, you see the test that ran after its last edit, or a flag that nobody checked.

items.title: ccstitch
items.line: A local trace viewer for Claude Code. It repairs the orphaned spans from claude-code#99607 and nests claude -p runs under the tool call that started them.

items.title: claude-code-behavior-specs
items.line: Three Claude Code CLI bugs I hit running agents headless. Each has a repro script and the workaround I shipped.

items.title: warden
items.line: Lets an agent fix things on its own only when the fix can be undone and a check proves it worked. Rolls back on failure. 28 offline tests.

items.title: recruit-copilot
items.line: A Claude Code plugin for a job search. It tailors a resume for each posting, checks the PDF a machine will read, and never submits. Truthfully I hate filling in job applications.

items.title: agent-evals-starter
items.line: A support-agent eval that runs offline. It includes a do-nothing agent and a do-anything agent, to show when a passing score means nothing.

groups.title: BYU AI Foundry
groups.lede: I founded the Foundry in 2025 and run it. Student teams build the products with real clients. These are the 3 AI products shipped so far, plus the Claude Code plugins the teams build with.

items.title: BYU AI Foundry
items.line: A program at BYU Marriott where student teams build AI products for real clients. 30 student builders. I'm the founder and managing director.

items.title: LawGrader and WriteGrader
items.line: Grading for legal and academic writing. It drafts the scores and margin comments. The instructor decides every final grade.

items.title: French 80/20
items.line: A French learning app for web and iPhone, built around the words you actually use.

items.title: CareBridge Connect
items.line: Turns the notes nursing-home staff already write into plain-language updates for approved family members. Onboarding its first customers.

items.title: AI Foundry Marketplace
items.line: The Claude Code plugins Foundry teams build with. Each skill is labeled by how well it has been tested. Install with one /plugin command.

groups.title: Siemens, and client work
groups.lede: My summer 2026 work at Siemens, and paid consulting I've done for a software company.

items.title: Spark AI at Siemens
items.line: An internal tool that installs a library of Claude Code agents, each set up for one job. My manager had the idea. I built it and demoed it live to the team.

items.title: Fable Software
items.line: Paid consulting for Fable Software. Live products from that work include SpeedPrep, ReadyStack and Deckboard.
